max_tire.note: Doesn't rub unless the springs have sagged (IH8MUD). Needs the 7-inch rims: ExplorOz owners say it's too wide for the 6-inch base rims.
Rubs with or without a lift, on the upper control arm and a rear pinch weld that can be ground down (IH8MUD).
Taller and lighter than a 285/75 and easier on the front end, but it needs a lift. Above 2–3 in, plan on a diff drop to protect the CVs.

timeline.change: J90 launched in Japan (8 May): three-door and five-door, 5VZ-FE V6 and 1KZ-TE diesel, full-time 4WD
Australian launch, petrol engines only; Britain gets it as the Land Cruiser Colorado
Facelift: multi-reflector headlights, clear lenses, new grille and dash, Active TRC; VSC on main auto grades from August; TX Limited edition
Sofasa begins assembling the J90 in Colombia
Australia finally gets a diesel: 96 kW 1KZ-TE with a five-speed manual (automatic from October)
1KD-FTV common-rail D-4D (170 PS, 352 Nm) replaces the 1KZ-TE in Japan, its first application
Replaced by the Prado 120 (Colombian production continues to 2009)

identify.intro: Every US J90 is a gray import, and the model code tells you what you're buying. Make sure the code on the paperwork matches the engine and body in front of you.

items.head: Model code = engine + body
items.body: VZJ = 3.4 V6, RZJ = 2.7 four, KZJ = 1KZ-TE diesel, KDJ = 1KD-FTV diesel. 90 is the three-door, 95 the five-door. Japanese codes carry a 'W' suffix (e.g. VZJ95W).

items.head: 1KZ or 1KD?
items.body: Toyota fitted the common-rail 1KD-FTV from July 2000 in Japan, so a KDJ95 should be a mid-2000-or-later truck. 4X4 Australia lists the Australian J90 diesel as the 1KZ-TE, from March 2000.

items.head: Pre- or post-facelift
items.body: Trucks built after the June 1999 minor change have large multi-reflector headlights, clear-lens indicators and a revised grille and bumper. Five-doors grew from 4,675 mm to 4,690 mm.

items.head: Japanese grades
items.body: Japanese three-door grades start with R (RZ, RX) and five-door grades with T (TZ, TX, TX Limited). Australian five-doors were sold as RV, RV6, GXL and VX Grande.

items.head: Lockers
items.body: Every J90 has a center-diff lock. Australian trucks had no factory axle lockers, so an ad claiming 'factory lockers' needs proof.

paragraphs: Toyota never sold the J90 in the United States; America got its platform twin, the [[4runner/3rd-gen|3rd-gen 4Runner]], instead. Every US Prado 90 is a gray import. NHTSA says a vehicle at least 25 years old can be lawfully imported without regard to whether it meets US safety standards, and that the 25 years run from the date of manufacture. A manufacture label, a first-sale invoice or an old registration document can prove it.

J90 production began in May 1996, so the first trucks became eligible in May 2021, and the last 2002 builds qualify during 2027. On the EPA side, Form 3520-1 code E covers vehicles at least 21 years old in original, unmodified configuration (an engine swap only qualifies if it's the same engine model). That makes a J90 federally straightforward. State titling, inspection and emissions are separate, and California is the hardest, so check your state's rules before you buy.

production.intro: Built by Toyota in Japan from 1996 to 2002, and assembled in Colombia for seven years after that.
